test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 30 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Where was the Hindu college established in the year 1791 to teach ancient Sanskrit texts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Banaras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu College was established in **1791 in Banaras (modern-day Varanasi)** by the efforts of Jonathan Duncan, the British Resident of Banaras.
 
• The college aimed to **promote the study of ancient Sanskrit texts** and traditional Hindu learning.
 
• It was later renamed as the **Government Sanskrit College** and eventually became an important center of learning for classical Indian texts.
 
• The institution was primarily focused on teaching subjects like **philosophy, grammar, literature, and law** in Sanskrit.
 
• The Hindu College in Banaras is considered a forerunner to institutions like the **Benares Hindu University (BHU).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Banaras (Varanasi)**

 
 
• Banaras, also known as Varanasi, is one of the **oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world**.
 
• It has been a major center for religion, culture, and education for centuries, particularly for Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit Education in Ancient India**
 
 
• Sanskrit was the primary language of instruction in ancient Indian education systems.
 
• Subjects like philosophy, astronomy, mathematics, and medicine were taught using Sanskrit texts.
 
 
 
• **Jonathan Duncan**
 
 
• Jonathan Duncan was a British administrator who served as the Resident of Banaras from 1788 to 1795.
 
• He played a significant role in promoting Sanskrit education and setting up the Hindu College in Banaras.
 
 
 
• **Modern Education Evolution**
 
 
• The Hindu College of Banaras laid the foundation for modern educational institutions in India, such as the Benares Hindu University (BHU), established by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1916.
 
• These institutions continue to contribute to the preservation and study of ancient Indian texts and traditions.
